subject: Termination recourse & performance security — Cygnus request
messages:
From: Anya Petrov <anya@cygnushealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Cygnus Health Procurement <procurement@cygnushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: termination rights + monetary remedies beyond credits

Markus —

Thanks for the conversation last week. Cygnus is preparing for FDA integration audits and our safety/compliance team has flagged the need for stronger commercial recourse if service-side availability or tail latency degrades repeatedly. High-level ask: we need a contractual path to financial remedies beyond service credits — specifically a capped fee-at-risk (liquidated damages) and the ability to terminate for repeated P1 outages.

Why: our product is used in clinical triage; downtime or severe latency spikes (P1) create regulatory exposure. Credits alone don’t offset audit risk or remediation costs.

What we’re proposing (initial):
- Termination right if 3 severity-1 incidents occur within a rolling 90-day period
- Fee-at-risk equal to up to 12 months of SaaS spend (or a fixed $ cap) payable as liquidated damages after cure fails
- An escrowed reserve or security deposit to make the remedy practical and immediate
- Evidence: 2 years of audit logs and error traces retained for our compliance team

We realize this is outside Redwood’s standard commercial posture — we’re sending this early in procurement to understand if you can make exceptions for regulated customers, and if so on what terms. I’ve attached a short annotated SLA (Cygnus_SLA_annotated.pdf) showing sections we care about.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through options?

Thanks,
Anya Petrov
Head of Procurement, Cygnus Health
anya@cygnushealth.com

Anya —

Appreciate the clarity and the annotated SLA — that was helpful. Quick thoughts before we loop legal:

1) We understand the regulatory exposure and want to be pragmatic.
2) Liquidated damages and termination rights are material changes to our standard SaaS terms; we’ll need to engage Legal + Revenue Ops.
3) Operational alternatives that reduce risk and may remove the need for onerous monetary remedies: dedicated cluster, accelerated incident review process, extended log retention, and an escrowed reserve that scales with MRR.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll run this with Legal and get back with a list of negotiable levers (caps, cure periods, exclusions).

We want to move quickly — you’re right that credits alone may not satisfy audit teams.

Subject: Fwd: Cygnus — termination recourse ask

Team — forwarding Cygnus’ ask. High level: they want termination rights for repeated P1s and a liquidated-damages style fee beyond credits. They cited regulatory exposure and want a practical escrow to cover remedies.

My read: we should avoid open-ended LDs; acceptable approach for Redwood would be a capped monetary remedy tied to MRR, a staged cure period, and operational commitments (dedicated infra + 2y logs). Legal will push back on termination triggers that are subjective, so propose we:

- Offer a capped fee-at-risk = up to 6 months of committed MRR (negotiable), payable only after a 90-day cure window following the final P1 in the series.
- Allow termination only after cure fails and after an independent post-incident review (to avoid gaming).
- Exclude force majeure, customer misconfiguration, and DDoS from triggers.
- Require a technical annex: dedicated GPU pool, mandatory monitoring hooks, 2-year log retention, and quarterly SRE review calls.

If Legal accepts that framework we can present it as a compromise: it gives them financial recourse and a termination path, but caps our exposure and ties remedy to operational fixes.

Thoughts? If you’re comfortable I’ll bring this to Legal and draft language.

—Markus

Markus —

Thanks for the quick follow. We reviewed your compromise proposal internally and are prepared to move toward an agreement if a few items are adjusted:

1) Cap: Cygnus prefers a cap at 12 months MRR rather than 6 — this reflects our audit remediation cost assumptions. If Redwood cannot commit to 12 months, we can accept 9 months as a possible middle ground.
2) Trigger timing: we need the ability to terminate after 3 P1s in a rolling 90-day window if Redwood fails to remediate within the cure period. The independent post-incident review is acceptable but must be completed within 21 days of the third incident.
3) Escrow: we want an escrowed reserve equal to 3 months MRR that can be drawn against to pay immediate remediation costs; the remainder of the cap is payable after legal determination.
4) Logs: 2 years retention and access for compliance auditors (read-only) with standard NDAs.

If you can draft these points into redlineable language we’ll circulate to our counsel. We’d like to keep this tight — can you send a redline by EOD Friday (11/19)? Also, please include a DocuSign packet for the addendum if legal is comfortable.

Happy to discuss on a call tomorrow at 10am PT if that helps.

Best,
Anya
Head of Procurement, Cygnus Health
